comment: Sound palettes (SoundPalette): a named sound world for a whole track — what a deck plays its track with, chosen per track (the `tracks` override `palette`, the poke DeckAction.setPalette) and carried into every new track the deck makes (Next, auto-next, the seed wheel, Wander). For each role (bass, melody, harmony, arp, stinger; `*` = any other tonal role; `kit` = the drums) a pool of options; a track plays one, picked by the track seed + role (`Project.applySound`); a role missing from `roles` plays its instrument's own sound, as Studio. Options: `own` (the instrument's own sound: its installed sampled instrument, else its synth voice) · `synth` (its synth voice, no sample) · `synth:<instrument>` (beats' synth voice of another instrument, Resources/voices/instruments.json; for `kit`, one of beats' synth kits: drums, drums-808, drums-cr78, drums-lofi, drums-v8, drums-breakbeat) · `cat:<category>` (an installed sound of a categories.json category, seeded, then the category's GM programs from the SoundFonts) · `gm:<program>` (a General MIDI program, 0-based, from the SoundFont folder: MuseScore_General.sf2 is the floor) · `dls:<program>` (Apple's gs_instruments.dls: local only, never published) · `bank:<bankCategory>` (categories.json bankCategories: the Minecraft bank, local only) · `inst:<instrument>` (play as if that instrument were picked) · for `kit` also a DrumKits id (`file#bank:program`). Options whose sound isn't installed are left out of the pick; a role with none left makes the palette unavailable, with the reason. `hints`: `room` / `echo` borrow another genre's reverb and echo (SpaceSpec / EchoSpec.forGenre; `none` = dry). `neighbours`: where Wander's palette hop may go. `default` is the palette a track without one plays (no override written).

studio.label: Studio
studio.description: Each instrument's own sound: the sampled instrument this Mac has for it, else beats' synth voice — how tracks sounded before palettes.

synth.label: Synth
synth.description: Beats' own synth voices on every part and its synth kits: no samples at all, the sound of the browser.

synthwave.label: Synthwave
synthwave.description: Analog polysynths: PWM and sync leads, warm pads, rubbery FM bass, an 808 or CR-78 under a long bright hall.

chiptune.label: 8-bit
chiptune.description: Square and pulse waves like a game console's sound chip, a tight dry room and a little machine kit.

acoustic.label: Acoustic band
acoustic.description: A band in a room: piano and guitars, electric or upright bass, organ chords and a real drum kit.

orchestral.label: Orchestral
orchestral.description: Cinematic: strings and brass, contrabass and cellos underneath, harp and pizzicato figures, timpani hits in a big hall.

lofi.label: Lo-fi tape
lofi.description: Dusty keys: Rhodes and Wurli, mellow bass, tape flutes and mallets over a soft kit, in a small dark room with a short echo.

jazz.label: Jazz club
jazz.description: A small group late at night: upright bass, piano or Rhodes comping, sax, muted trumpet or jazz guitar on top, brushes on the kit.

club.label: Club
club.description: House and techno: acid and reese basses, rave stabs and organ chords, plucks, on 909-style or 808 drum machines in a tight room.

ambient.label: Ambient
ambient.description: Slow and wide: evolving pads and choirs, bells and mallets, a sub bass, soft drums, a long room and a slow echo.

world.label: World strings
world.description: Plucked and bowed strings from around the world: guzheng, koto, pipa, erhu, sitar and banjo, with flutes, harp and a room kit.

retro.label: 90s sound card
retro.description: General MIDI the way a computer played it: every part and the kit from Apple's own GM bank (gs_instruments.dls). Local only: never published.

minecraft.label: Minecraft
minecraft.description: The game's note blocks, bells and goat horns, built on this Mac from your own installed game (make minecraft). Local only: never published.
